arxiv-2012-08951.title: SimuGAN: Unsupervised forward modeling and optimal design of a LIDAR Camera
arxiv-2012-08951.creator: Nir Diamant, Tal Mund, Ohad Menashe, Aviad Zabatani, Alex M. Bronstein
arxiv-2012-08951.description: Abstract Energy-saving LIDAR camera for short distances estimates an object’s distance using temporally intensity-coded laser light pulses and calculates the maximum correlation with the back-scattered pulse. Though on low power, the backs-scattered pulse is noisy and unstable, which leads to inaccurate and unreliable depth estimation.

arxiv-2102-10556.title: Inductive logic programming at 30 Journal: Machine learning
arxiv-2102-10556.creator: Andrew Cropper, Sebastijan Dumančić, Richard Evans, Stephen H. Muggleton
arxiv-2102-10556.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Andrew Cropper, Sebastijan Dumančić, Richard Evans, Stephen H. Muggleton. Inductive logic programming (ILP) is a form of logic-based machine learning. The goal is to induce a hypothesis (a logic program) that generalises given training examples. As ILP turns 30, we review the last decade of research. We focus on (i) new meta-level search methods, (ii) techniques for learning recursive programs, (iii) new approaches for predicate invention, and (iv) the use of different technologies.

arxiv-2107-04156.title: Theory of Vibrational Polariton Chemistry in the Collective Coupling Regime
arxiv-2107-04156.creator: Arkajit Mandal, Xinyang Li, Pengfei Huo
arxiv-2107-04156.description: Abstract We theoretically demonstrate that chemical reaction rate constant can be significantly suppressed by coupling molecular vibrations with an optical cavity, exhibiting both the collective coupling effect and the cavity-frequency modification of the rate constant. When a reaction coordinate is strongly coupled to the solvent molecules, the reaction rate constant is reduced due to the dynamical caging effect.

arxiv-2211-05188.title: Etude des ( n + 1 ) (n+1) -tissus de courbes en dimension n n
arxiv-2211-05188.creator: Jean-Paul Dufour et Daniel Lehmann
arxiv-2211-05188.description: Abstract For ( n + 1 ) (n+1) -webs by curves in an ambiant n n -dimensional manifold, we first define a generalization of the well known Blaschke curvature of the dimension two, which vanishes iff the web has the maximum possible rank which is one.

arxiv-2510-12094.title: H4G: Unlocking Faithful Inference for Zero-Shot Graph Learning in Hyperbolic Space DOI: XXXXXXX.XXXXXXX ISBN: 978-1-4503-XXXX-X/2018/06 CCS: Information systems Data mining
arxiv-2510-12094.creator: Heng Zhang, Tianyi Zhang, Zijun Liu, Yuling Shi, Yaomin Shen, Haochen You, Haichuan Hu, Lubin Gan, Jin Huang
arxiv-2510-12094.description: Abstract . Text-attributed graphs are widely used across domains, offering rich opportunities for zero-shot learning via graph-text alignment. However, existing methods struggle with tasks requiring fine-grained pattern recognition, particularly on heterophilic graphs. Through empirical and theoretical analysis, we identify an over-abstraction problem : current approaches operate at excessively large hyperbolic radii, compressing multi-scale structural information into uniform high-level abstractions.

arxiv-2511-17489.title: Harnessing Data from Clustered LQR Systems: Personalized and Collaborative Policy Optimization
arxiv-2511-17489.creator: Vinay Kanakeri, Shivam Bajaj, Ashwin Verma, Vijay Gupta, Aritra Mitra
arxiv-2511-17489.description: Abstract It is known that reinforcement learning (RL) is data-hungry. To improve sample-efficiency of RL, it has been proposed that the learning algorithm utilize data from ‘approximately similar’ processes. However, since the process models are unknown, identifying which other processes are similar poses a challenge.

pmc-10643089.title: Post-COVID-19 syndrome: Descriptive analysis based on a survivors' cohort in Colombia
pmc-10643089.creator: Martin Romero, Martha Caicedo, Andrea Díaz, Delia Ortega, Claudia Llanos, Alejandro Concha, Andrés Vallejo, Fernando Valdés, César González
pmc-10643089.description: BackgroundThe prevalence of post-COVID-19 Syndrome (PCS) is estimated to be between 10% and 20%. The main reported symptoms are fatigue, memory alterations, dyspnea, sleep disorders, arthralgia, anxiety, taste alterations, coughing and depression. This study aims to determine the prevalence of post-COVID-19 symptoms in a group of Colombian patients who were recruited during their outpatient appointments.

pmc-11346466.title: Anisotropic DBSCAN for 3D SMLM Data Clustering
pmc-11346466.creator: Pilar Lörzing, Philipp Schake, Michael Schlierf
pmc-11346466.description: Single-molecule localization microscopy (SMLM) advanced biological discoveries beyond the diffraction limit. Various implementations enable 3D SMLM to reconstruct volumetric cell images. Yet, the inherent anisotropic point spread function of optical microscopes often limits the localization precision in the axial direction compared to the lateral precision. Such localization anisotropy could also expand spherical cellular structures to ellipsoidal cellular structures.

pmc-11367504.title: Proteus syndrome with progressive paralysis of the unilateral lower limb: A rare case report and literature review
pmc-11367504.creator: Feng Cai, Zhi Liu, Jun Zou, Yunfeng Liu, Weiming Tang, Liping Zhou, Xiaojian Zhu, Xiaoping Huang, Wei Long, Shushan Zhao
pmc-11367504.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). ObjectiveProteus syndrome, a rare disorder with an incidence of one in a million, is characterized by connective tissue nevi, asymmetric limb overgrowth, and abnormal subcutaneous adipose tissue distribution. Limited awareness of this condition often hinders accurate clinical diagnosis. We report a case of Proteus syndrome with concurrent progressive paralysis in the unilateral lower limb, aiming to enhance understanding of the disease and its associated complications.MethodsThe patient, an 11-year-old male, has been conclusively diagnosed with Proteus Syndrome.

pmc-12657293.title: Clinical translation of TLR agonist-modified silicified cancer cell therapy supported by humanized mouse models
pmc-12657293.creator: Mara P. Steinkamp, Danielle Burke, Madigan Morrison, Irina Lagutina, Lillian Fitzpatrick, Rita E. Serda
pmc-12657293.description: Humanized patient-derived xenograft (huPDX) mouse models are crucial for evaluating the clinical translation of new immune therapeutics. Silicification of cancer cells renders the cells non-viable with enhanced stability and silica surface functionalization, enabling adsorption of pathogen-associated molecular patterns to attract and activate myeloid cells.

pmc-12770468.title: Question asking practice fosters aspects of curiosity in science content in young children
pmc-12770468.creator: Anne T Park, Joseph Colantonio, Lourdes Delgado Reyes, Sophie D S Sharp, Andrew E Koepp, Elizabeth Bonawitz, Allyson P Mackey
pmc-12770468.description: Children who are more curious learn more in school, but little is known about how to promote curiosity-driven behaviors. In a preregistered experiment, 103 children (54 boys, 49 girls, ages 5–7 years) were randomly assigned to a condition in which they were encouraged to ask questions, or to listen carefully, during eight one-on-one science lessons over 2 weeks.

pmc-13199398.title: Quaternized cellulose nanofibril paper coatings for sustainable packaging with improved barrier and antibacterial performance
pmc-13199398.creator: Yoon-hyuck Choi, Seungmin Han, Soo-jeong Shin, Zhenghui Shen, Araz Rajabi-Abhari, Jaeho Ryu, Wanhee Im
pmc-13199398.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Quaternized cellulose nanofibrils (quaternized CNFs) with different cationic group contents were prepared and applied as multilayer paper coatings to develop sustainable antibacterial and barrier materials. Increasing the cationic group content (160–660 µmol/g) reduced CED viscosity and yield stress, indicating weakened network structures and reduced interfibrillar interactions These rheological changes improved coating flow and layer uniformity, leading to denser coating layers with enhanced air barrier performance and water resistance.

pmc-13235942.title: Accurate computation of ionic concentrations in the synaptic cleft requires the full Poisson–Nernst–Planck (PNP) equations
pmc-13235942.creator: Karoline Horgmo Jæger, Aslak Tveito, Alain Nogaret, Alain Nogaret, Alain Nogaret
pmc-13235942.description: The synaptic cleft between neighboring neurons is the site of neurotransmitter-mediated communication that underlies normal brain function, including learning and memory. When an action potential reaches the presynaptic terminal, released neurotransmitters cross the cleft under the combined influence of diffusion and electrical forces to activate postsynaptic receptors.

pmc-13585250.title: Inflammation is associated with altered functional connectivity of the cingulate cortex in individuals with subthreshold depression
pmc-13585250.creator: Zhangzhang Qi, Pan Chen, Guanmao Chen, Zhenye Luo, Shu Zhang, Lijun Jiang, Guixian Tang, Li Huang, Qian Tao, Ying Wang
pmc-13585250.description: Subthreshold depression (StD) represents a critical prodromal phase that often precedes clinical depression. Identifying biological indicators during this stage is essential for the prophylaxis of major depressive disorder. The present study investigated the interplay between serum pro-inflammatory cytokines, functional connectivity (FC) within subregions of the cingulate cortex (CC), and psychometric profiles in an StD cohort.

pmc-13610688.title: Early-Life Nutrition: The Interplay of Nutritional, Microbial, Genetic, and Environmental Factors in Food Allergy Development and Prevention
pmc-13610688.creator: Maria Rogalidou, Tania Siahanidou
pmc-13610688.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Background: Food allergy is an important health concern, particularly during infancy and early childhood. Its development reflects complex interactions between genetic susceptibility and early-life nutritional, microbial, epithelial, immunological, and environmental factors. Objective: To examine the role of early-life nutrition in the development and prevention of food allergy, with emphasis on its interplay with the gut microbiome, genetic and epigenetic susceptibility, epithelial barrier function, and environmental exposures.
